articles/ecs-architecture.html.title: ECS Architecture | AWEngine
articles/ecs-architecture.html.summary: ECS Architecture AWEngine uses the ECS pattern to separate data and logic. All examples are just examples, and they are written to be AS SIMPLE AS POSSIBLE. EcsEntity EcsEntity is a unique container for components. It has methods such as: EcsEntity.AddComponent(EcsComponent component) Adds a component to the entity. Supports method chaining (EcsEntity.AddComponent(EcsComponent component).AddComponent(EcsComponent component)). EcsEntity.RemoveComponent<T>() where T : EcsComponent Removes a component from the entity. Also supports method chaining. EcsEntity.SwapComponent<T>(EcsComponent S) where T : EcsComponent Replaces component T with component S. Added so you don't have to write "remove this component and add that component" twice. EcsEntity.GetComponent<T>() where T : EcsComponent Gets component T from the entity to work with its contents. EcsEntity.HasComponent<T>() where T : EcsComponent Returns true if component T exists in the entity. Example with EcsEntity: var hero = new EcsEntity(); hero.AddComponent(new Info { Name = "Hero", Description = "Really cool guy"} ); hero.AddComponent(new Respect()); hero.AddComponent(new Inventory { Space = 10 } ); if (2+2 != 5) { hero.SwapComponent<Respect>(new Disrespect()); } if (hero.HasComponent<Respect>()) { hero.GetComponent<Inventory>().Space = 20 } else { hero.RemoveComponent<Inventory>(); } EcsComponent EcsComponent represents pure data (inherits from EcsComponent). Example with EcsComponent: public class Respect : EcsComponent //You can even leave them empty if you want to use them as a marker, or honestly, just do whatever you want. { } public class Inventory : EcsComponent { public int Space { get; set; } } EcsSystem EcsSystem handles game logic processing entities. Registered via SystemManager by execution phases (ExecutionPhase). Child classes MUST implement public override void Update(IReadOnlyList<EcsEntity> entities). Example with EcsSystem: public class AOEDamage : EcsSystem { public override void Update(IReadOnlyList<EcsEntity> entities) { var mainHero = entities.FirstOrDefault(s => s.HasComponent<MainHero>()); foreach(EcsEntity entity in entities) { if (entity.HasComponent<Enemy>()) { entity.GetComponent<Stats>().HP -= mainHero.GetComponent<Stats>().AOEDamage } } } } WorldContext WorldContext is the storage for all active entities (EcsEntity) in the world. It has the following methods: WorldContext.AddEntity(EcsEntity entity) Adds a new entity to the storage. WorldContext.Cleanup<T>() where T : EcsComponent Deletes all entities that have component T (for example, if you created a Remove component, all entities having this component will be deleted when this method is called). Example with WorldContext: var wc = new WorldContext(); var hero = new EcsEntity(); var enemy = new EcsEntity(); hero.AddComponent(new MainHero()).AddComponent(new Stats{ HP = 100, Damage = 50}); enemy.AddComponent(new Enemy()).AddComponent(new Stats{ HP = 30, Damage = 15}); wc.AddEntity(hero); wc.AddEntity(enemy); var mainHero = wc.Entities.FirstOrDefault(s => s.HasComponent<MainHero>()); var enemy = wc.Entities.FirstOrDefault(s => s.HasComponent<Enemy>()); if(enemy.GetComponent<Stats>().HP - mainHero.GetComponent<Stats>().Damage <= 0) { enemy.AddComponent(new Remove()); } else { Console.WriteLine("Enemy: ez"); } wc.Cleanup<Remove>(); SystemManager SystemManager is the storage for all registered systems (EcsSystem) sorted by execution phases (ExecutionPhase). It has methods: SystemManager.Add(ExecutionPhase phase, EcsSystem system) Adds a system to the list for a specific execution phase type. Supports overloading and can accept a List<EcsSystem> instead of a single system. SystemManager.Remove(ExecutionPhase phase, EcsSystem system) Removes a system from the list for a specific execution phase type. SystemManager.Update(WorldContext wc, ExecutionPhase phase) Executes all registered systems for the specified execution phase type. Example with SystemManager: public static class GameSystems { public static ExecutionPhase render = new ExecutionPhase(); public static ExecutionPhase input = new ExecutionPhase(); } var wc = new WorldContext(); var sm = new SystemManager(); systems.Add(GameSystems.input, new GetButton()); systems.Add(GameSystems.render, new MainMenu()); var ui = new Entity(); ui.AddComponent(new MainMenuUI()) wc.AddEntity(ui); sm.Update(wc, GameSystems.input); sm.Update(wc, GameSystems.render);

articles/engine-lifecycle.html.title: Lifecycle and Errors | AWEngine
articles/engine-lifecycle.html.summary: Lifecycle and Errors The Run(bool FastSplash = false) method manages the engine's full lifecycle, sequentially guiding the application through initialization, the main loop, and safe interception of potential crashes. Execution Order Splash Screen (SplashScreen) Displays the engine's start screen. Behavior depends on the FastSplash parameter: false (default): Displays the signature ASCII art, authorship info (AWEngine by revDevotee), and launches an animated loading spinner (-, \, |, /). true: Skips the animation and ASCII art, displaying a short text string with a 1.5-second delay for a faster startup. Initialization (Init) Calls the protected abstract Init() method. At this stage, the child class is required to implement all necessary user-defined preparation (loading resources, creating starting entities, etc.). Main Loop (Update) Launches a continuous process within a while (running) block. Iterations run as long as the running flag is true. Modifying this flag from the outside allows for a graceful shutdown of the engine. Critical Error Handling The entire engine lifecycle (from the splash screen to the completion of Update) is wrapped in a protective try-catch block, preventing sudden application crashes without logging: If any unhandled exception (Exception ex) occurs, the console is cleared (Console.Clear()). The engine generates and prints a structured critical error report: [SOURCE] — source of the error (assembly/module). [TYPE] — full name of the exception class. [MESSAGE] — error message. [STACKTRACE] — detailed call stack trace. Program execution is paused until the user presses any key (Console.ReadKey()), allowing them to review the crash details. [Note] A bit later, I’ll make it return an error instead of write it in console.

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | AWEngine
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started To get started with AWEngine, you need to create a class that inherits from the abstract AWEngine class and implement the mandatory Init() and Update() methods. But of course, you can choose not to use my methods and write your own loop and stuff, and the only thing you'll lose is the splash screen and simple error output :c Use my method. Please 😭😭😭 Example of a minimal project using System; using AWEngine; class Program { static void Main(string[] args) { MyGame game = new MyGame(); // Run engine(FastSplash: true, if you want to skip splash screen faster. False by default) game.Run(FastSplash: false); } } public class MyGame : AWEngine.AWEngine { protected override void Init() { Console.WriteLine("Loading game..."); // Here you can create entity, systems, and register them in worldcontext and systemmanager, or uhh anything you want } protected override void Update() { // Main game cycle Console.WriteLine("Game loaded, maybe"); // if you want to exit game, you can change this state to false(true by default) running = false; } } SplashScreen The engine supports a colorful splash screen. You can trigger it manually, or it will run automatically when calling the Run() method: FastSplash = false - displays a full ASCII-art banner and an animated initialization process with a spinner (-, , |, /). FastSplash = true - fast text output for 1.5 seconds.

index.html.title: AWEngine Documentation | AWEngine
index.html.summary: AWEngine Documentation AWEngine is a lightweight, custom C# game engine implementing the ECS (Entity-Component-System) pattern, made by revDevotee. All rights are NOT reserved! :D Key Features Custom ECS Architecture: Flexible separation of data (EcsComponent, EcsEntity) and logic (EcsSystem). Execution Phases: Control system execution order via SystemManager. (Un)reliable Error Handling: Built-in exception handling mechanisms operating at both the engine game loop level and isolated within each system. Navigation Quick Start — how to launch a project using AWEngine. ECS Architecture — deep dive into entities, components, and systems. Lifecycle & Error Handling — how the main loop works and crash protection works. Still Confused? I mean, everything should be crystal clear, but feel free to try asking me if you get stuck ;D
